# EDN Core Behavioral Specification

## 1. Scope

The EDN core module is the distribution point in the entropy distribution network. It receives random bit blocks from a CSRNG application interface and distributes them as 32-bit words to peripheral endpoints.

The module does not generate entropy. It is responsible for:

- forwarding CSRNG application commands,
- receiving random blocks from CSRNG,
- buffering and partitioning those blocks into 32-bit endpoint words,
- serving endpoint requests,
- reporting FIPS status for distributed data,
- detecting and reporting fatal and recoverable errors,
- providing interrupt and alert indications.

This specification describes the observable behavior of the EDN core module only.

---

## 2. Functional Overview

The module supports up to four endpoint ports. Each endpoint receives random data using a request/acknowledge handshake and a 32-bit data bus. A FIPS indicator accompanies the data.

The module also provides a software-visible command path. Firmware can issue CSRNG commands, and the module forwards those commands to the CSRNG interface. The module can also issue commands automatically in two hardware-controlled modes:

- boot-time request mode,
- auto request mode.

In all modes, random data returned by the CSRNG is distributed only to the endpoint ports.

---

## 3. Reset and Disabled State

After reset, the module shall be disabled. While disabled, the module shall:

- not issue any CSRNG command requests,
- not acknowledge endpoint requests,
- clear all pending command and data output paths,
- deassert endpoint FIPS indicators,
- not accept software command requests.

The module shall become operational only after firmware enables it through the control interface. While disabled, endpoint requests must be ignored and no random data shall be delivered.

---

## 4. Endpoint Data Distribution

### 4.1 Request/Acknowledge Behavior

Each endpoint requests a fresh 32-bit word by asserting its request input. The module shall respond as follows:

- If a 32-bit word is available for that endpoint, the module shall drive that word on the endpoint data bus and assert the acknowledge output.
- If no word is available, the module shall hold acknowledge low. The endpoint must wait until data becomes available.
- A word is consumed when the endpoint’s request and the module’s acknowledge are both asserted in the same cycle.
- The data bus shall remain stable after an acknowledge. It shall not change until a new word is delivered to that endpoint.
- If an endpoint does not request data, data already delivered to that endpoint shall remain available and unchanged.

### 4.2 Arbitrating Among Endpoints

Multiple endpoints may request data at the same time. The module shall arbitrate among requesting endpoints and deliver one 32-bit word to one endpoint at a time. Each request shall eventually be served when data is available.

The module shall apply backpressure to the CSRNG random-data interface when endpoint buffers are full and no endpoint can accept more data.

### 4.3 FIPS Indicator

Each endpoint shall have a FIPS indicator that describes the quality of the random data currently being delivered.

The FIPS indicator shall:

- be asserted when the associated CSRNG random block was produced from a FIPS-approved state,
- be deasserted when the random block was produced from a non-FIPS or pre-FIPS state,
- be deasserted when the endpoint data path is cleared or reset.

The FIPS indicator shall be updated when a new random block is made available to the endpoint. It shall be associated with the same data source as the word on the endpoint data bus.

---

## 5. CSRNG Application Interface Behavior

The module shall send CSRNG command words to the CSRNG application interface. The command words originate from one of the following sources:

- a software command request,
- the boot-time instantiate command register,
- the boot-time generate command register,
- the reseed command queue,
- the generate command queue.

The module shall forward command words exactly as provided by the selected source. It shall not modify the command contents.

The module shall hold a command word on the CSRNG command output until the CSRNG indicates that it has accepted the command.

The module shall accept random blocks from the CSRNG only when it has storage or endpoint demand available. If endpoint data buffers are full, the module shall signal the CSRNG not to send additional random data.

When the CSRNG returns a command status response, the module shall capture that status for firmware and may generate a command-request-done interrupt.

---

## 6. Command Modes

### 6.1 Software Command Forwarding

In software command operation, firmware writes a CSRNG command to the software command request register. The module shall:

1. present that command to the CSRNG interface,
2. wait for the CSRNG command status response,
3. store the returned status,
4. report command completion.

The module shall provide a ready status indicating whether the software command port can accept a new command. The ready status shall be deasserted while a software command is being processed and shall be reasserted when the next command can be accepted.

Firmware shall only write a new software command when the ready status indicates that the command port is available.

### 6.2 Boot-Time Request Mode

Boot-time request mode provides automatic command generation with no firmware command customization.

When boot-time request mode is selected and the module is enabled, the module shall:

1. issue a boot instantiate command,
2. then issue boot generate commands repeatedly,
3. continue issuing boot generate commands until the module is disabled or boot-time request mode is deselected.

The boot instantiate and boot generate commands shall be taken from the configured boot command registers.

Boot-time request mode shall take precedence over auto request mode. If both modes are selected, the module shall operate in boot-time request mode.

Random data returned during boot-time request mode shall be distributed to endpoints using the normal endpoint distribution behavior. Endpoint FIPS indicators shall reflect whether the CSRNG data source is FIPS-approved.

### 6.3 Auto Request Mode

Auto request mode is used to continuously provide entropy to endpoints without firmware involvement after initial configuration.

Before auto request mode can operate, firmware must first instantiate the CSRNG instance and load the required commands into the reseed and generate command queues.

When auto request mode is selected and the module is enabled, the module shall:

- issue generate commands from the generate command queue,
- issue reseed commands from the reseed command queue,
- alternate between these commands according to the configured maximum number of generate requests between reseeds,
- continue automatically until the module is disabled, auto request mode is deselected, or the module is reset.

The module shall count generate commands issued. When the count reaches the configured maximum, the module shall issue a reseed command, reload the count, and resume generating.

Commands loaded into the generate and reseed command queues shall be reused. Issuing a command shall not permanently remove it from its queue.

If auto request mode requires a command and the corresponding command queue is empty, the module shall report a fatal error.

### 6.4 Mode Transitions

When leaving boot-time request mode or auto request mode, the module shall stop issuing new automatic commands. Any CSRNG command currently in progress shall be allowed to complete before the module reports that the mode transition is complete.

Firmware shall not reconfigure or load new commands until the module has completed the current command sequence and is idle.

---

## 7. Command Queue and Data Buffer Behavior

The module shall maintain separate queues for reseed commands and generate commands. These queues are loaded by firmware and read by the automatic command state machines.

The module shall also maintain an output path for commands that are ready to be sent to the CSRNG interface.

The module shall support resetting the command queues through the control interface. When a command queue reset is requested, the queue contents shall be cleared.

The module shall detect and report the following command queue errors:

- writing to a queue that is already full,
- reading from a queue that is empty,
- a queue reporting an internally inconsistent state, such as appearing both full and empty.

These errors shall be treated as fatal errors.

---

## 8. Fatal Error Detection and Reporting

The module shall detect fatal errors in the following categories:

- command queue write errors,
- command queue read errors,
- command queue state errors,
- main control state machine integrity errors,
- endpoint acknowledge state machine integrity errors,
- counter integrity errors,
- any error injected through the error test interface.

When a fatal error is detected, the module shall:

- assert the fatal alert output,
- assert the fatal error interrupt,
- set the corresponding fatal error status bit or bits.

Fatal state machine and counter errors shall be reported regardless of whether the module is enabled.

Fatal errors caused by command queue overflows, underflows, or state inconsistencies shall be reported when the module is enabled.

The module shall provide a fatal alert test capability. Firmware can trigger a fatal alert test through the alert test interface.

---

## 9. Recoverable Error Detection and Reporting

The module shall detect recoverable errors in the following categories:

- invalid encoding of a protected control field,
- a repeated random data pattern on the CSRNG data path.

### 9.1 Invalid Control Field Encoding

The module protects certain control fields with multi-bit encoding. If firmware writes an invalid encoding, the module shall:

- reject the invalid value,
- set the corresponding recoverable alert status bit,
- continue operating with the previous valid value if one exists.

### 9.2 Repeated Random Data Detection

The module shall check the random data blocks returned by the CSRNG for a repeated-data condition. If two consecutive random blocks delivered to endpoints have the same low 64 bits, the module shall treat this as a recoverable error.

When this condition is detected, the module shall:

- assert the recoverable alert output,
- set the data consistency status bit.

This detection is a security countermeasure and shall not affect the data already delivered to endpoints.

The module shall provide a recoverable alert test capability. Firmware can trigger a recoverable alert test through the alert test interface.

---

## 10. Interrupt Behavior

### 10.1 Command Request Done Interrupt

The command request done interrupt shall be generated when the CSRNG returns an acknowledgment for a command that is being reported to software.

The interrupt shall be cleared by software through the interrupt state register. It shall be masked by the corresponding interrupt enable bit.

### 10.2 Fatal Error Interrupt

The fatal error interrupt shall be generated when any fatal error condition is detected.

The fatal error interrupt shall be asserted for fatal state machine errors and counter errors regardless of module enable state.

The fatal error interrupt shall be asserted for command queue errors when the module is enabled.

The interrupt shall be cleared by software through the interrupt state register. It shall be masked by the corresponding interrupt enable bit.

---

## 11. Status and Error Reporting

The module shall provide software-visible status information for:

- software command ready,
- command completion status returned by the CSRNG,
- command queue error conditions,
- main state machine state,
- endpoint state machine errors,
- counter errors,
- recoverable alert conditions,
- invalid control field encodings.

Error status bits shall be sticky. Once set, they shall remain set until explicitly cleared by software. The module shall set each error bit only when the corresponding error condition is detected.

The module shall provide an error test capability that allows firmware to force specific error status bits for validation. This test capability shall only affect reported status and alert/interrupt generation; it shall not alter normal data behavior.

---

## 12. Initialization Sequence

The recommended initialization sequence is:

1. Reset the module.
2. Configure the entropy source and CSRNG as required by the system.
3. Enable the EDN module in the desired mode.
4. If using auto request mode, instantiate the CSRNG instance and load the command queues before enabling auto request mode.

In boot-time request mode, no software command queue loading is required. The module shall begin issuing boot commands immediately after being enabled.

For auto request mode, firmware must ensure the CSRNG instance is already instantiated and the command queues are loaded before enabling the mode.

---

## 13. Summary of Required Behaviors

- Distribute CSRNG random data as 32-bit words to up to four endpoints.
- Use request/acknowledge handshakes with stable data buses.
- Provide FIPS indicators for endpoint data.
- Forward software CSRNG commands and report completion.
- Support boot-time request mode and auto request mode.
- Enforce the configured reseed interval in auto request mode.
- Detect command queue, state machine, counter, and configuration errors.
- Detect repeated random data blocks.
- Assert fatal alerts and fatal interrupts for fatal errors.
- Assert recoverable alerts and status for recoverable errors.
- Provide interrupt and alert test capabilities.
